summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease with prior amputations, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for cough, nausea, and nocturnal hypoxia. His blood pressure was elevated on presentation but improved with medication. He was found to have oxygen desaturation during sleep, consistent with his known sleep apnea, which he had not been treating due to CPAP discomfort. A plan was made with the sleep team to initiate nocturnal home oxygen at 3 liters per minute instead of PAP therapy, given concern for complex sleep apnea. His kidney function remained stable, tacrolimus levels were therapeutic, and his other chronic conditions were managed without change. He was discharged home the following day with arranged oxygen delivery and plans for outpatient follow-up with sleep and nephrology specialists.
